newsitem.title: UK: British jobless total falls 68,200 in February.
newsitem.headline: British jobless total falls 68,200 in February.

text.p: Britain's jobless total fell 68,200 to 1.75 million in February, leaving 6.2 percent of the working population without a job, official data showed on Wednesday.
Retail sales, a key indicator of consumer confidence, rose 0.5 percent in February, the statistics office said.

The figures, although leaked overnight to the tabloid Mirror newspaper, were a boost to Prime Minister John Major at the start of the May 1 election campaign. The jobless total has now fallen for 12 months in a row.
Government bonds fell sharply after data showed average earnings rose 5.0 percent in January, a figure higher than expected.
Analysts said the strong figures increased the pressure for a rise in interest rates, currently at 6.0 percent, to dampen inflationary pressures.
Philip Shaw, economist at Union PLC, said the data "suggest that there is a need for a modest tightening of monetary policy."
